newsitem.title: FRANCE: Ex-mayor of Lyon in new French sleaze probe.
newsitem.headline: Ex-mayor of Lyon in new French sleaze probe.

text.p: Former mayor of Lyon Michel Noir is being probed again for sleaze in a case in which he received a suspended 18-month prison term last year, French justice sources said on Thursday.

Noir, a former member of parliament and trade minister once tipped as a possible presidential candidate, was formally placed under investigation on Wednesday on suspicion of receiving misappropriated company funds, the sources said.

Judge Gilbert Emery questioned Noir for five hours concerning 10 million francs ($1.75 million) deposited by three business executives -- who are also under investigation -- into Swiss bank accounts held by his son-in-law Pierre Botton.

Botton, who served a three-and-a-half-year jail sentence for embezzling corporate funds and funnelling them to Noir, testified in the earlier case that the money in the Swiss accounts was secretly used to pay Noir's expenses.
Noir has consistently denied the allegations.

Noir has also previously been convicted of diverting eight million francs ($1.4 million) of Lyon's municipal funds to finance political campaigns and personal expenses. He was given a 12-month suspended sentence in that case.
